title: `round(d)`: `op(x · 10ᵈ) / 10ᵈ`, no negative `d`
verdict: matches the reference on the edge cases; `d < 0` refused
description: `round(d)` multiplies by `10ᵈ`, rounds (half to even unless `mode` says otherwise) and divides back; from `d = 300` it splits the multiplier into powers of 2 and 5, from `d = 326` it returns the input, and a non-finite intermediate returns the input. The two roundings make ties of the decimal text round either way: `round(2.675, 2)` is 2.68 though the double is below 2.675, and `round(0.285, 2)` is 0.28.
A negative `d` is refused by the Python API (`OverflowError`, `decimals` is a `u32`).
reference: `round` to `d` digits (#335), `TIE_AWAY_FROM_ZERO`, with negative digits. On the probe's edge cases at `d` = 1, 2, 16, 308, 309, 400 Polars and the reference agree.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
